Only in Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206): The divine warning commands: abandon riches, spurn property and save life; After the flood all humankind has returned to clay; the plain is flat as a roof; Instead of the flood, a lion, a wolf, famine or plague should have diminished the people; The mother goddess bars the god who caused the flood from the offering, for he acted without counsel; Huge measured quantities of bitumen, pitch and oil are poured into the kiln and the hull; The hero slaughters oxen and sheep and gives the workers beer, oil and wine like river water, so they feast as at the New Year festival; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer; The chief god sees the boat and is enraged that a living being escaped: 'no man should survive!'; What the ark contains; Besides kin and animals, craftsmen of every skill are taken aboard; The god gives the hero a cover story: Enlil hates me, I am going down to the Apsû, and he will rain abundance on you (bread-cakes in the morning, a torrent of wheat in the evening) - an ambiguous promise of the coming flood; How the ark is described; and 78 more.

Only in Al-Qamar: the moon split, the dead like locusts, and Noah's ark of planks and fibres: God left the ark (or the event) as a sign: is there anyone who will remember?; God opens the gates of heaven with pouring water and makes the earth burst with springs; the waters meet for a decreed matter; Noah, called a madman and driven off, prays 'I am overcome, so help me!'; Whenever they see a sign they turn away and say 'continuous/passing sorcery' (sihr mustamirr); What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; With downcast eyes they come out of the graves like scattered locusts, hastening to the caller; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; Heaven is opened (its udders or its gates) to release water [divergence between the texts]; 'The Hour has drawn near and the moon is split' (inshaqqa l-qamar); A great multitude spread over the land is likened to locusts (irby / jarād); A multitude rising or pouring out is likened to a swarm of locusts; God opens the windows or gates of heaven, for blessing or for the flood [contrast between the texts]; and 11 more.

Only in Kirugu 5: Enlil calls the storm; fire, darkness and the sunless day cover Urim like a cloak (Lament for Urim 172-206): The high god hands the destroying storm over to a divine storm-keeper or enlists the fire god as its helper; The destroying storm-wind wrecks the land by its god's command; The day of YHWH's anger on which none escape; The word or pronouncement of the high gods (An, Enlil) is itself the force that destroys the city; The destroying storm covers the city like a cloak and is spread over it like a linen sheet; In the catastrophe the sun god sets and does not rise again; The god's decreed destruction is a 'deluge' (amaru, abubu) or storm that sweeps over the land, used of invading armies; God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven; Humanity or the Sumerians called 'the black-headed'; A Sumerian song divided into numbered kirugu sections, each followed by a ĝišgiĝal antiphon.

Only in Refrains over 'Ad, Thamud's she-camel, Lot's guests and Pharaoh; everything by measure; the seat of truth: God's command is but one, like a blink of the eye; The guilty are dragged on their faces into the Fire: 'Taste the touch of Saqar'; The God-fearing are in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth with an all-powerful King; A single Cry (sayha) is sent and they become like the dry stubble of a pen-builder; When they solicited Lot's guests, God obliterated their eyes; 'The host will be routed and turn their backs' (applied to Badr); The high god's command is spoken once only: not twice, not turned back; Everything they did is in the scriptures (zubur); every small and great thing is written down; God created everything by measure/decree (bi-qadar); 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; Supernatural being must leave before daybreak; and 14 more.
